# Lab 11 — Layouts in memory and on the wire

**Unit:** [week 11, systems programming I: data in memory](../../week11-layouts.md)
(exercises 1 and 4). **Time:** 2 hours. **Runs in the playground:** yes

The same three fields take 24, 16 or 13 bytes depending on their order and
on the layout attribute. You minimise a `@repr(C)` struct, then write an
encoder and a decoder for the `@packed` wire format in safe code.

## Start

- [Open the starter in the playground](https://fides-lang.org/playground#), or
- copy [`starter.fd`](starter.fd): `fid run starter.fd`.

Embed:

```html
<iframe src="https://fides-lang.org/playground/embed.html#"
        width="100%" height="420" style="border:0" title="Lab 11 starter"></iframe>
```

## Tasks

1. **Reorder.** Reorder `Header`'s fields so that its `@repr(C)` size is
   as small as possible, and state the rule you used. `struct_size` checks
   it.
2. **Encode.** Write `encode(h: Header) -> Vec<u8>`: the 13 bytes of the
   `@packed` layout (`tag`, then `len`, then `id`), each field
   little-endian, without `unsafe`.
3. **Decode.** Write `decode(b: &Vec<u8>) -> Option<Header>`, `None`
   unless there are exactly 13 bytes. Check that `decode(encode(h))`
   gives `h` back for zeros, 255, `0xffffffff` and `2^40`, and that a
   one-byte buffer is rejected.

## Check your work

When you are done, `fid run starter.fd` prints:

```text
Header: 16 bytes
Wire:   13 bytes
encoded: 07 01 02 00 00 ff ff ff ff 00 00 00 00
zeros: ok
255s: ok
0xffffffff: ok
2^40: ok
1 byte: rejected
```

## Questions to hand in

- Draw the 16-byte `Header` and the 24-byte one byte by byte. Where is the
  padding, and why must the size be a multiple of 8?
- `encode` reads `h.id as i64`. Which `id` values would that break, and how
  would you encode a full `u64`?
